practiceReport.name: Drake Maye
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (88% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

practiceReport.name: A.J. Brown
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Coming out of a Week 11 bye, Brown didn't take any reps during the two bonus practices the Patriots held Monday and Tuesday, so it comes as little surprise that he was absent from the team's first official practice of Week 12. Head coach Mike Vrabel has already acknowledged that Brown isn't expected to play Sunday versus the Chargers, but the Patriots will likely wait until after Friday's practice before officially ruling the receiver out for that contest.

practiceReport.name: Walter Rouse
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (OL) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
factors: Remains in early stages of NFL 5-Step Concussion Protocol
practiceReport.beatComment: Rouse is in the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing in Week 10 against the Lions in Munich. Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice. Even if he practices over the coming days, an independent neurologist would need to clear Rouse from protocol in order for him to be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

practiceReport.name: Carlton Davis III
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (8th NFL season, 87% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday; remains sidelined from practice
practiceReport.beatComment: Davis didn't travel with the Patriots to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. Even with the extra rest courtesy of the bye, Davis has not been cleared by medical staff to return to practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a realistic shot of playing Sunday against the Chargers.

practiceReport.beatComment: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

practiceReport.name: Ben Brown
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (C) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Brown did not play in the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Lions in Munich due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. With a full practice under his belt, Brown is on track to play against the Chargers on Sunday and should reclaim his starting spot at left guard while Walter Rouse reverts to a depth role on the offensive line.

irAndReserveTracker.name: TreVeyon Henderson
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 11 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Dell Pettus
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Pettus exited the second quarter of Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers with an ankle injury, and he'll now have to miss at least the next four games while on IR. With Craig Woodson (shoulder) also injured, the team will likely look to sign or elevate a player from the practice squad for Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Jaguars.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Harold Landry III
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Landry spent the entirety of training camp and the preseason on the active/PUP list with an undisclosed injury. The 30-year-old will now be sidelined for at least four contests to open the 2026 campaign, and the earliest he'd be able to return to action is Week 5 against the Raiders on Oct. 11. In his absence, Elijah Ponder is a top candidate to start opposite of Dre'Mont Jones at outside linebacker.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Khalil Jacobs
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Jacobs participated in the first two preseason games for the Patriots before succumbing to injury, accumulating eight tackles (four solo). The linebacker will need to miss the first four games of the regular season on IR before he is eligible to return to the active roster. While Jacobs is sidelined, Darius Muasau will likely be the first depth option behind starting inside linebackers Christian Elliss and Robert Spillane.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mike Onwenu
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle in the Patriots' win over the Steelers on Sunday, and he appears likely to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Greg Van Roten is likely the next man up at right guard for New England.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Quintayvious Hutchins
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hutchins appeared in both of the Patriots' first two games of the 2026 campaign, accumulating three total tackles. The rookie will now miss at least four games while tending to a knee injury. While Hutchins has played sparingly, his absence will still allow Gabe Jacas and Jose Ramirez to see a little more action.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Julian Hill
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hill joined the Patriots back in March on a three-year deal, but an unspecified injury now will sideline the tight end for the season. For now, Eli Raridon, CJ Dippre and Tanner Arkin are in the mix behind top TE Hunter Henry, but there's a solid chance the team will bring in added depth at the position in the wake of Hill's injury.
